headline: Merz surprise Kyiv visit with €1bn military aid; Houthis claim Aramco Riyadh strike.

stories.title: Merz surprise visit to Kyiv — €1bn military + €350m energy
facts: Chancellor Merz arrived Sunday morning by special train with Economy Minister Katherina Reiche and ~10 defence/energy executives.
Government circles: ~€1bn already-approved military funds (thousands of interceptor drones vs Russian jet-powered Shaheds) + ~€350m for energy-plant repairs.
Joint long-range weapons (>1,000 km) production to be pushed; Merz: if Russia is not stopped, it will turn its war machine against Europe "sooner or later".
Fifth war winter; Russian MFA had warned diplomats away from Kyiv hours earlier.
stories.whyItMatters: A surprise Sunday presence in Kyiv with drone/energy packages and industry CEOs signals Berlin’s wartime industrial track, not just another photo-op.

image.alt: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is greeted in Kyiv on Sunday morning

stories.title: Houthis claim Aramco strike near Riyadh as Yemen fighting intensifies
facts: Sat: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed ballistic missiles and drones hit an Aramco facility in Riyadh; smoke/flames seen near the site (AFP photos).
Saudi-led coalition spokesman called the Riyadh-targeting claim "misleading".
Early Sun: coalition claimed 97 ops on Tor al-Baha / Taiz axes; truce collapse since July; Bab al-Mandeb / Mocha shipping context.
stories.whyItMatters: Even a disputed claim on Riyadh energy infrastructure keeps Red Sea / Gulf oil risk in play while Yemen fighting escalates.

image.alt: Houthis claim strike on Aramco site as Yemen fighting intensifies

stories.title: Reiche pushes Rentenreform decision by year-end vs Bas
facts: BamS interview (ZEIT/dpa ~03:15): Economy Minister Katherina Reiche wants pension reform passed this year; Bas should table a draft quickly.
Warns against watering down Rentenkommission elements; open fight includes abschlagsfreie Rente nach 45 Jahren ("Rente mit 63").
Interior Minister Dobrindt said disputes are to be cleared "in the next days".
stories.whyItMatters: Coalition pension timing pressure lands the same weekend Reiche accompanies Merz to Kyiv — domestic fiscal politics stay live.

stories.title: Federal judge: Flock ALPR is "indiscriminate mass surveillance"
facts: Judge Sara Hill (N.D. Okla.): Tulsa deputy’s warrantless Flock plate search violated the Fourth Amendment; evidence suppressed.
First-ish federal finding that a Flock search was unconstitutional (not binding precedent).
Sen. Sanders introduced a "Block Flock Act"; some FL/TX jurisdictions pulling back; Flock offering buyouts.
stories.whyItMatters: A federal suppression ruling against Flock’s ALPR dragnet raises the legal temperature on mass plate tracking beyond local politics.

stories.title: Altman: ascribing religion to models is a safety issue
facts: Sat: Sam Altman said he is "very uncomfortable" with religious force / surrender of human judgment to models — framing it as a safety issue.
Contrasts with Anthropic/Olah outreach to religious leaders on consciousness and moral behaviour (NYT earlier in the week).
DeepMind’s Jon Barron also critical ("Team Meatbag").
stories.whyItMatters: Fresh overnight AI beat distinct from Fri’s Robinson resign / agent-review costs — consciousness-and-faith framing is now a safety talking point.

SOS-Kinderdörfer + Terre des Hommes: kids not adequately protected from AI; regulation lagging (ZEIT).
